core.title: Keep every source file at a 10% or higher comment ratio
core.given: An in-scope production source file (a file of the profile's source kinds), not a test file, not under a vendored or build-output tree, changed or not
core.when: its comment lines fall below 10% of its non-blank lines
core.then: Raise the file's comment ratio to at least 10% by writing down the decisions and constraints invisible to a reader.
prefer: Diagnose: module purpose and owned responsibility; non-obvious invariants, upstream/compatibility constraints, failure semantics; obvious implementations intentionally not chosen.
Document why a choice exists, which invariant a block keeps, or which external constraint forces the shape.
Use a concise module/GREEN header giving real purpose and runtime context; with a few explanatory lines it clears the floor.
Place the explanation next to the decision it clarifies.
avoid: Comments restating the next line of code.
Filler, generated prose, repeated headings, or artificially split comment lines to raise the ratio.
Commenting out dead code instead of deleting it.
Changing cohesive code solely to manipulate the denominator.
Stale or misleading comments; any behavior change (tests stay green).
unless: Unit test, acceptance test and e2e test files; vendored and build-output trees (outside the scan).
core.why: Comment-free files almost always hide unwritten non-obvious decisions. 10% is a floor against absence, not a quality measure or prose quota; numerator-padding filler makes the source worse.
evidence: The comment-ratio finding is gone for the file.
Every added comment conveys information not already obvious from the code.
No stale or misleading comments were introduced.
Behavior remains unchanged and tests stay green.
The refactor introduces no new violations of this stack's ATDD convention checks.
verification: comment_ratio = comment lines / all non-blank lines; threshold: ratio >= 0.10 for every in-scope source file (the profile's source kinds).

Comment lines are recognized per the stack's syntax, using the profile's comment-line forms — line comments, block comments, and continuation lines inside a block comment — counted against all non-blank lines.
Blank lines are excluded from both numerator and denominator.

The scan covers every in-scope source file, changed or not. Test files and vendored/build trees are outside the scan; the exact exclusion set (including the exact classification of test files and of vendored/build trees) is owned by the stack's checker, not by this rule.
Ten percent is low enough that any file with a real header and a few explanatory lines clears it.

The ratio cannot tell a good comment from a bad one; it is a floor against absence (floor_against_absence), catching the file that documents nothing. Reviewers judge whether added comments carry real design context and flag filler or restating comments added to game the numerator. Treat the ratio as a sensor for missing design context, not a prose quota; a successful repair leaves readers information the code itself cannot communicate.
Severity 2; disposition strict: fails on every finding; no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

fires: Any scanned production source file that is not a test file and not under a vendored/build tree has comment lines under 10% of its non-blank lines, whether or not it was edited in this task.
The metrics check reports a below-floor comment-ratio finding for a non-test, non-vendored, non-build source file in the scanned tree.
A new non-test source module outside vendored/build trees is written whose comment lines are below 10% of its non-blank lines.
doesNotFire: A unit test, acceptance test or e2e test file has no comments.
A file under a vendored or build-output tree has a low comment ratio.
A source file already at or above a 10% comment ratio, regardless of whether its comments are a header or explanatory (quality is a review concern, not this trigger).
Files of other kinds (configuration, markup, data files, other languages) — only the profile's source kinds are scanned.

neutralityNotes: The 10% floor, the strict disposition and severity 2 stay in the core: they are the obligation and rule metadata, not stack data. The comment-line recognition forms ('line, block, `*` continuations') are stack syntax and could not be expressed with the closed vocabulary (idiom.comment_marker covers only line comments), so they are proposed as idiom.source_syntax#comment_line_kinds. Vendored/build trees are profile data under roots.excluded (bun.json's examples are kept explicitly illustrative and non-exhaustive), while the general test exemption stays in the core (unit/acceptance/e2e test roles): bun.json's illustrative test-file globs and its deference to the detector's authoritative exclusion set are realization details, and the checker-owned exact classification lives only in core verification. The 'module/GREEN header' wording is kept because GREEN is a methodology term, not a stack term. The title/given '.ts/.tsx' specifics become the profile's source kinds; finding and detector ids are bunOnly.
